commits.subject: Box the future returned by response item injection (#62420)
commits.reason: Adopt the boxed Core response-item injection future and retain the fork’s batch admission across native mailbox delivery.
evidence: The public method now returns BoxFuture tied to the borrowed thread. Its inner async method receives the same items, and its entire upstream body is byte-identical across the change. The single Core integration test binary also raises its recursion limit to 256.

The cumulative fork keeps admit_upgrade_input inside the native plaintext mailbox branch, before pin_v2_residency and the loop of per-message submissions. Raw, mixed and encrypted inputs still take the retained history path. A three-commit merge rehearsal preserves both the new inner method and this fork hook.
commits.revisit: Run the Core agent_mailbox integration cases for interrupted sampling and idle eviction, and the native handoff controls for already accepted input.

commits.subject: Reject provider query parameters for connector result passthrough (#62421)
commits.reason: Adopt the narrower Responses destination check for optional private connector results across configured routes and refreshed credentials.
evidence: HTTP sampling resolves the destination from the current credential owner, a ChatGPT credential variant, internal metadata policy, the approved gateway, permitted provider headers, empty request-specific headers and absent or empty provider query parameters. The retained owner still verifies the connector grant.

The client setup fixture exercises refresh, custom destination, internal metadata and header exclusions. The enterprise lifecycle fixture verifies its configured provider still receives its account bearer and ordinary executed-call metadata. The direct-system-proxy change is a test fixture. The fork’s foreground credential-attempt recorder and transport recovery remain in the composed source.
commits.revisit: Run client_setup_rebuilds_chatgpt_refresh_but_rejects_account_switches and enterprise_lifecycle_preserves_history_and_ordinary_tools. Include a changed provider query map on the approved origin and check that sampling omits result bodies.

commits.subject: Include nested Apps tool results in Code Mode sampling requests (#62423)
commits.reason: Carry nested Apps result passthrough behind the existing connector feature, analytics consent and provider metadata policy. Preserve the fork’s packaged defaults.
evidence: Nested Code Mode dispatch binds the projected result and nested call ID to their originating turn and exec or wait output. Capture checks the connector credentials at dispatch and completion. A weak turn handle, owner checks and bounded byte accounting constrain the original private payload.

The recorder invalidates result bindings and refunds budget on replacement, pruning, conflicting calls and untrusted output. HTTP sampling appends the body and JSON-escaped call ID together only when both fit. The in-memory request enrichment leaves persisted conversation history and the ordinary WebSocket frame unchanged.

The former direct-only condition from #62392 now permits eligible nested Apps calls. Neither ALab packaged defaults file enables connector_tool_result_passthrough. The bounded three-commit merge rehearsal preserves the fork’s task assignment admission and request-credential hooks.
commits.revisit: Run nested_call_id_and_result_fit_the_wire_budget_together, nested_result_budget_reopens_after_binding_loss, direct_result_body_budget_reopens_when_the_output_is_lost and the direct and Code Mode cases of result_metadata_preserves_results_within_request_budget. Exercise disabled analytics, changed credentials and same-turn replacement alongside the private wire capture.
